title: Failure of finite assembly for a chromatic overlap at the prime three
main_claim: At p=n=3, L_2 L_{K(3)} S is not in Thick{L_0S, L_1S, L_2S} in E(2)-local S-modules. Proof outline: a mod-3 detector V_d(X) = pi_d L_{K(2)}(E_2 ^ X)/3 tensored with k((x)) is shown to have only periodicity-power constituents on the thick closure of L_{K(2)}S. A descent spectral sequence then produces a norm-twisted line Q_x(delta) in V_{-3}(L_{K(3)}S_k). The SS has a finite abutment filtration and its E_2 rows sit in s=0,1 (trivial) and s=3,4 (twisted by delta).
coverage:
This was a third, partial pass, with Sections 2, 8, 9 and 10 read in full. Checks that hold:
- Prop 2.x: the Serre-subcategory closure under triangles, and V_d of the K(2)-local unit.
- Thm main reduction: L_{K(2)} kills L_0S and L_1S; S_k is finite free, so Z_k is a finite sum of copies of L_{K(3)}S.
- Lemma 10.1, verified step by step:
  - The kernel of the G_F action on k[[x]] lies in Z_3^x, and O_F^x/Z_3^x is infinite.
  - The fixed-field argument via Weierstrass finiteness gives fixed field k.
  - The Hasse section h = a1 (dT)^2 is invariant with v_x = 1, which forces the parity 2v(f) = b.
  - Q_x(delta) is nontrivial because k is relatively algebraically closed in k((x)).
- E_2/abutment bookkeeping: with d_r of bidegree (r, r-1), only d_3 can occur, from row 0 to 3 or 1 to 4. Its target is delta tensor omega^{j+1}, which the lemma excludes. In the (s,t)=(3,0) term, d=-3 gives exactly Q_x(delta).
- Prop 8.x: the finite-cube model for Tot_r plus Mathew's nilpotence bound gives a finite filtration (F^{N+1}=0) on the actual homotopy, and the diagonal idempotent commutes with it.
- Lemma 8.x cooperations: comparing coefficients gives ca=0 and ct=c^{p^2}, so the right ring is k((t)).
- Lemma 9.1: the deformation-torsor rank is rank Hom(omega_{G^vee}, Lie G) = 2·1, matching Omega^1_A of rank 2. P/J equivariance follows from rigidity and uniqueness of lifts.

Not line-checked:
- Sections 4–7 (perfectoid/v-stack towers, the analytic orientation computation, decompletion via Cartier finiteness).
- Theorem 7.x's statement that ordinary H^*(P, L) has four lines with ell|_{O_F^x} = delta.
Everything rests on these as black-box inputs.
sibling_notes: Earlier passes on this paper (rank 202, 1st and 2nd) also found no gap; my checks agree with theirs. One observation: by Prop 10.x, every V_d(L_{K(2)}L_{K(3)}S) has dimension 2 over Q_x. The split form L_{K(2)}(S v S^{-1}) would give dimension 1. So the paper also implicitly refutes the chromatic-splitting shape at p=n=3. That is consistent with the intro's remark that a strong decomposition would imply finite assembly. Companion Rational/Filtered papers are not used in the proof (the intro says so, and I confirmed it). The critical external input is the BMR26 exceptional branch p-1 | h-1. The whole result rests on the unverified Section 6–7 computation that H^3 and H^4 of P with coefficients in L are lines carrying the delta character.
